reader.requirement: A comma or semicolon immediately followed by a space is a separator accepted wherever the separator space may stand (between any two character-strings, in every division, in headers, clauses, statements, lists and compiler-directing COPY/REPLACE text), except that a comma inside a PICTURE character-string is a PICTURE symbol; a comma or semicolon not followed by a space is no separator.
reader.edition-search: grep -i 'edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion' over SeparatorRule.cs (its summary: edition-invariant) and CobolLexer.g4 with its superclass Parsing/CobolLexerBase.cs (only the case-mapping spelling and the reference-paren word set, neither touching ', '/'; '); the separator rules FNARG_SEPARATOR, PIC_WS, SEMICOLON carry no predicate on the edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: lists, subscripts, reference modifiers, qualifiers and the PICTURE boundary; not exercised: division/section headers, ENVIRONMENT and FILE SECTION clauses, level numbers, 88 VALUE THRU, statement keyword pairs (GO, TO; STOP, RUN), COPY ... REPLACING and REPLACE text, DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, a separator comma at line end

probes.expected: accepted: ', ' and '; ' in IDENTIFICATION, DIVISION, SELECT, ASSIGN, FD, level numbers, PIC, 9(3), VALUE, 88 VALUE, 1, THRU; 3, OCCURS, MOVE, IF/ELSE, ADD GIVING, OPEN, PERFORM, 2, TIMES, GO, TO; STOP, RUN; PIC 9,999 keeps its comma
COPY, CPYA; REPLACING, ==CPY-X==, BY; ==CPY-Y== and REPLACE, ==XX==; BY, ==N== applied; DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA literal 1,5 with 'TO XX, M' separator

probes.printed: COBOL2631 the comma is not immediately followed by a space, so it is not a separator
probes.expected: ADD A,B refused: a comma without a following space is no separator

reader.notes: The lexer skips ', '/'; ' exactly as a space outside list regions and keeps it only as an item boundary inside one (CobolLexerBase.ListItemBoundary); PIC_WS and OnPictureString keep a comma inside the PICTURE string. The preprocessor treats the separator as a space when matching. No edition switch on the path; the COBOL2631 refusal text cites §1985:IV.4.2.1 SR2 at --std 85.
